brief: Cold outreach: before vs after automation

slots.title: Cold outreach is broken.
slots.description: Six months ago every reply was a coin flip. Here is what changed, step by step, with the numbers.

slots.title: Stop cleaning lists.
slots.description: Manual list building ate the first three hours of every day and still shipped duplicates.
slots.badText: Export, dedupe, guess the title, paste into the sheet, repeat tomorrow.
slots.goodText: Filters run overnight and the qualified list is waiting before the first coffee.
slots.ctaArrow: One filter replaced the whole ritual

slots.title: Stop guessing fit.
slots.description: Half the pipeline was people who were never going to buy, and nobody found out until the third email.
slots.badText: Anyone with the right job title went straight into the sequence.
slots.goodText: Company size, stack, and live intent decide who is worth a message at all.
slots.ctaArrow: Disqualifying early is the whole trick

slots.title: Stop sending templates.
slots.description: The same opener went to a seed founder and a bank. Both ignored it, and both were right to.
slots.badText: One template, a merge field for the first name, and hope.
slots.goodText: Three angles drawn from what the company actually shipped this quarter.

slots.title: Stop forgetting.
slots.description: Follow-up happened when someone remembered, which meant it mostly did not happen.
slots.badText: Two touches, then the thread quietly died in a busy week.
slots.goodText: Six touches on schedule, paused the moment a human actually replies.
slots.ctaArrow: Most deals are lost to silence

slots.title: Stop reading every reply.
slots.description: Hot replies sat unread next to out-of-office bounces until the end of the week.
slots.badText: One inbox, everything mixed together, triaged whenever there was a gap.
slots.goodText: Intent gets classified on arrival and the buyers land straight on the calendar.
slots.ctaArrow: Speed is most of the advantage

slots.title: Stop guessing what worked.
slots.description: Nobody could say which step was leaking, so every fix was a guess dressed up as a strategy.
slots.badText: A gut feeling about the pipeline and a spreadsheet nobody updated.
slots.goodText: One page every Monday naming the bottleneck in plain words.
slots.ctaArrow: You cannot fix what you cannot see

slots.body: None of this needed a bigger team. It needed the boring parts to stop depending on somebody remembering.
slots.ctaText: Comment outreach and I will send the build
